newsitem.title: USA: Gilead Forvade trial data insufficient.
newsitem.headline: Gilead Forvade trial data insufficient.

text.p: Gilead Sciences Inc said on Tuesday the U.S. FDA determined that data from a placebo-controlled Phase I/II clinical study were not sufficient to support marketing clearance for Forvade to treat refractory herpes simplex virus infection in AIDS patients.

After reviewing Gilead's new drug application seeking marketing clearance, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration sent the company a letter recommending additional studies to support clearance, Gilead said.
In January 1997, the FDA accepted the Forvade application for review, the company said.

The application included safety and efficacy data from a Phase I/II placebo-controlled study in 30 AIDS patients with refractory herpes lesions, who were randomly assigned to receive either Forvade, a topical cidofovir gel, at one of two dose levels or placebo once daily for five days, it said.
During the study, neither patients nor physicians knew if patients were receiving the active drug or placebo, Gilead said.

At two scientific conferences in 1996, investigators presented data from the Phase I/II study that demonstrated a statistically significant treatment effect with Forvade versus placebo in healing of refractory lesions, stopping viral shedding and reducting lesion-associated pain, the firm said.
Gilead Chief Executive John Martin said the company planned to work with the FDA to determine what additional information would be necessary for approval.
